inventory.visualPurpose: The seven-row drug class table (the section's sole printed element — the DRUGS × ORGAN SYSTEMS × APPLICATIONS grid of the muscarinic-antagonist class)
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: ONE SEVEN-ROW TEXT TABLE (PURE TEXT — ZERO rasters on pdf 262-263; pdfimages returns no rows; COPYRIGHTED, never reproduced as artwork). Three printed column headers: DRUGS / ORGAN SYSTEMS / APPLICATIONS. Seven rows: 'Atropine, homatropine, tropicamide' | Eye | 'Produce mydriasis and cycloplegia'; 'Benztropine, trihexyphenidyl' | CNS | 'Parkinson disease (“park my Benz”)' + 'Acute dystonia'; 'Glycopyrrolate' | GI, respiratory | 'Parenteral: preoperative use to reduce airway secretions' + 'Oral: reduces drooling, peptic ulcer'; 'Hyoscyamine, dicyclomine' | GI | 'Antispasmodics for irritable bowel syndrome'; 'Ipratropium, tiotropium' | Respiratory | 'COPD, asthma' + 'Duration: tiotropium > ipratropium'; 'Solifenacin, Oxybutynin, Flavoxate, Tolterodine' | Genitourinary | 'Reduce bladder spasms and urge urinary incontinence (overactive bladder)' + 'Make bladder SOFT'; 'Scopolamine' | CNS | 'Motion sickness'. The book's OWN mnemonics print inside the cells ('park my Benz', 'Make bladder SOFT'). Carried VERBATIM as the note's two table blocks and conveyed as ONE original KYP class map (the lock strip, the five organ-lane cards, the dry-mirror band, the antidote-mirror strip, the boundary strip, the reading-rule footer) — no artwork reproduced.
